section_summary.extract_value: This introduction reviews the development and validation of body image measurement instruments, particularly the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS) and its revised version (BAS-2). The section discusses the BAS's widespread use and strong psychometric properties, but highlights cross-cultural limitations in factorial equivalence across different populations. It then describes Tylka and Wood-Barcalow's (2015b) revision of the BAS into the BAS-2, which consists of 10 items and demonstrated one-dimensional factor structure invariant across participant sex in three studies with U.S. adults.

section_summary.extract_value: This introduction section discusses the development and validation of the Body Appreciation Scale-2 (BAS-2), a revised measure of positive body image. The text explains that the original BAS had cross-cultural limitations, leading Tylka and Wood-Barcalow (2015b) to develop the BAS-2 with 10 items. Table 1 presents the standardized item-factor loadings for the BAS-2 separately for women and men, showing how each item loads onto the body appreciation construct.
